finding: Pending-save handling: a save captures its note id and values when the user types. Switching notes, creating one, deleting one, or hiding the page flushes it first, so a delayed save can't land on the wrong note.

Shared-notes search: a new query aborts the old request, and the ctrl !== sharedCtrl check discards stale responses. A server error shows a message and leaves the local notes alone.

Not flagged: /api/shared has no server in this diff. The code treats a failing endpoint as an error state, so I did not call that a bug.

Validation (steps 5 and 6): with nothing flagged, there was nothing to validate or filter.

The agents did mention three behaviours that are not definite bugs, so I left them out:

Missing backend: The summary agent noted that the diff does not include the /api/shared backend the app calls. That is outside the diff and not a defect in it.

Nothing was posted and no files were changed.

store.js:50 Data with a version newer than SCHEMA_VERSION is read as v1 and written back as v1, and the stored version is never checked. A newer build, or another tab on a newer version, saves {version:2, notes:[{..., tags:[...]}]}. This build normalizes each note to only id, title, body and updated. The next edit saves it back as version 1, with no backup and no warning, so the extra fields and version are permanently lost.

They cannot switch to the second note and cannot delete any note. A touch user on a phone never sees the delete bin.

app.js:217 Every search query is sent to /api/shared without consent or disclosure. The request is also not cancelled when the shared box is hidden after a fetch fails. A user types private text into the 'Search notes' box meant for local notes. After 250ms the text goes to the server. There is no UI warning that the search leaves the browser.

app.js:119 flushSave() drops the pending edit if the save fails, and nothing retries it. Storage is full. flushSave sets pending=null, updates the note in memory and commit() shows the error. If the user does not act, no later flush retries the write. The data is only in memory and is lost on reload. The error status can also be overwritten by the next 'Saving…' or 'Saved'.

Bugs (2 opus agents): neither agent flagged a high-signal issue, so step 5 had nothing to validate. Both traced these paths and found them correct:
The delayed save writes to the note that was being edited.
Aborted shared-note searches are ignored.
Old saved notes load correctly, with a backup kept when data is unreadable.
User and server text never goes through innerHTML.

store.js:61 Migrated or normalized notes (new UUIDs for missing or duplicate ids, numeric ids turned into strings) are not saved back, so the ids change on every reload until the user edits something. Version-0 data contains two notes with id 1, or a note with no id. Each reload assigns fresh random ids to those notes. A delete or select that depends on stable ids is not reproducible between sessions, and the stored data stays in the old format until the first edit.

store.js:30 A failed backup of unreadable data is swallowed, and the load message still says the data was kept. store.js:30 ignores the result of the backup write. The three callers (store.js:47, :52, :66) then return messages that state the data 'was kept under notes-backup'. The comment says the load message covers a failing store, but none of those messages does: only the getItem-blocked branch at store.js:39 mentions storage. saveNotes (store.js:73) overwrites STORAGE_KEY on the next edit. STORAGE_KEY holds a 3 MB truncated JSON string (a half-finished write). Copying it to 'notes-backup' needs about 3 MB more, so the origin quota is exceeded and setItem throws QuotaExceededError. The catch drops the error. loadNotes returns 'Saved notes could not be read. The unreadable data was kept under "notes-backup".' The user clicks New note. saveNotes replaces STORAGE_KEY with a small valid object. The only copy of the old notes is gone, and the app told the user it was kept.

store.js:30 Backup failure is swallowed, yet the load message still says the unreadable data 'was kept'; the next save then overwrites it. backupRaw returns nothing and loadNotes ignores the outcome: store.js:47-48, 52-53 and 65-67 always return a problem sentence claiming the data 'was kept under notes-backup'. The comment says the message reports the failure, but the message text at those lines is unconditional. After the failed load, notes is [] and the first New note calls saveNotes (app.js:33), which replaces STORAGE_KEY, the only remaining copy. localStorage holds a large unreadable 'notes' value (for example 3 MB of truncated JSON) in a 5 MB quota. On load JSON.parse throws, setItem(BACKUP_KEY, raw) throws QuotaExceededError and is swallowed, and the user is told the data was kept under 'notes-backup'. The user presses New note; the small valid list replaces the original value. The recoverable data is gone and the message was false.

app.js:129 flushSave always reports 'Saved' and re-renders. When commit fails, the in-memory edit stays and pending is cleared, so nothing retries. The quota is full. The user types, flushSave runs and shows the error. They keep typing, and each later flush re-attempts the full save. If they navigate away or close the tab after a failed save, the edits are lost with only a transient error shown. The error status is also overwritten by 'Saving…' on the next keystroke, so the failure is easy to miss.
